headline: AI model gets a 32-bit RISC-V CPU compiled directly into its weights, then runs DOOM on it
summary: The experimental Qwenputer LLM can run C and MicroPython code and even DOOM on its integrated CPU, overcoming common arithmetic weaknesses of AI models.
details: AI engineer Divyansh Agrawal has developed Qwenputer, an experimental blend of the stock Qwen 3.5 4B LLM with a 32-bit RISC-V CPU compiled directly into its weights. This allows the AI to perform processor arithmetic operations and run C and MicroPython code.

A key innovation is the use of Qwen’s Gated DeltaNet (GND) state as RAM, which the developer describes as a "neat trick." While using 'fast weights' as RAM isn't entirely new, this specific modification to Qwen 3.5 appears to be a first.

Unlike traditional LLM creation, the RISC-V CPU implementation doesn't involve training. It consists of 11 transformer layers placed before Qwen's own, with all weights computed by a compiler rather than learned. The built-in CPU has successfully passed official RISC-V tests and run 18 million instructions without error.

The CPU inside Qwenputer enables exact calculations, directly addressing the arithmetic weaknesses often found in LLMs. Users can run code on this integrated CPU without needing external tools or runtime calls, demonstrating its functional integration.

Agrawal also extended the model by giving it a persistent filesystem, which was relatively simple to implement since RAM was already in place. This storage also utilizes the DeltaNet state, offering 1,024 slots for up to 512 files.

Due to its expanded capabilities, Qwenputer has nearly doubled the size of the underlying Qwen 3.5 4B LLM, growing to almost 19GB. Consequently, the current version requires a workstation with 24GB of VRAM or more for testing.

This project is experimental, primarily built to explore new possibilities rather than solve a specific problem. The code is MIT-licensed and available on GitHub, and the LLM can be downloaded from Hugging Face for those interested in experimenting.
